raw_response:
I'm 69 this year, been farming these 18 mu in Quzhou for 15 years now. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so most of the year it's just me and my wife in the fields. They come back for harvest and the busy spells. We keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, 5 mu of cotton, and 3 mu of chili. That mix has worked for us — if one crop has a bad year, the others usually pull us through.

The wheat went in last October around the 15th, after I ran the rotary tiller over the field. For this spring, I'll topdress about 8 kg of pure nitrogen per mu at jointing stage — that's roughly 17 kg of urea. The extension technician told me I could push it to 10 kg N per mu, but last year I used 8 kg and got about 450 kg per mu, and that's good enough for me. At my age I'm not chasing record yields, I'm chasing stability. I'll irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping water isn't cheap anymore with the electric meters, but cutting an irrigation to save 60 yuan and then losing 50 kg of grain — that's a bad trade. I'll spray herbicide once in spring and keep an eye out for powdery mildew.

For the maize, I plant it right after wheat harvest, usually June 8th to 12th. The window is tight — if you delay past June 15th, the yield drops, I've seen it happen to my neighbor. I'll buy hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu at roughly 40 yuan. At planting I'll put down compound fertilizer, about 35 kg per mu, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 10 kg urea per mu. That gives me around 15 kg N per mu total. I'll irrigate twice in summer if the rain doesn't come — once at jointing and once at grain filling. Herbicide and insecticide once each should be enough.

Cotton goes in around April 20th. I prepare the rows and apply base fertilizer — compound fertilizer about 30 kg per mu plus some urea, totaling about 12 kg N per mu. Cotton needs attention — I'll spray for bollworm, aphids, and mites about 5 times through the season. Two irrigations, one at flowering and one at boll stage. Harvest is September through October, picked three or four times. It's labor-intensive, so when my daughter-in-law comes back for autumn she helps with the picking. Otherwise we'd have to hire too many hands.

Chili is on 3 mu. I'll transplant seedlings in late April. Chili likes fertile soil — I'll use about 40 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, and topdress twice with urea during flowering and fruiting. Total N around 14 kg per mu. Three irrigations, and regular sprays for aphids and disease. The picking is the hard part — every few days during peak season. My wife handles most of it, and we hire some local women to help, otherwise we'd never get it all picked in time.

Total input costs this year will run about 7,500 yuan. I could probably save 500 yuan by cutting back on fertilizer, but at my age I'd rather be safe than sorry. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps. My neighbor down the road tried reducing his fertilizer last year and his wheat was visibly shorter at heading — no thank you. I've got some cash saved from my son's remittances, so I'm not cash-constrained, but I'm still careful. Every yuan has to earn its keep.
